desc.arc.extract_here: Extract next to the archive (a folder is created only when needed)
desc.arc.extract_to: Extract into a folder of your choice
desc.arc.list: Show the files inside, with sizes
desc.arc.test: Check that the archive is intact without extracting it
desc.arc.convert: Repack the archive in this format
desc.arc.protect_7z: Repack as 7z with AES-256: content and file names are encrypted
desc.arc.protect_zip: Repack as ZIP with AES-256 (file names stay visible)
desc.arc.unprotect: Repack the archive without its password
desc.arc.join: Join the .001, .002… parts into the original file
prm.arc.force.help: Skip the zip-bomb check (suspiciously high compression ratio).
prm.arc.smart.help: A single top-level item is extracted directly; otherwise a folder named after the archive is created.
err.arc.bomb: Suspicious archive: it would expand {ratio}× to {size}. Enable “Extract anyway” to continue.
err.arc.no_parts: The other parts were not found next to this file
err.arc.no_space: Not enough space to extract: {need} needed, {free} free
err.arc.not_archive: Not an archive, or an unsupported format
err.arc.password_format: {fmt} archives cannot have a password: use ZIP or 7z
err.arc.password_needed: The archive is password-protected: open the options (Alt) and type the password
err.arc.single_stream: This file holds a single compressed file: use Extract here
err.arc.unsafe: Unsafe archive: {n} entries point outside the destination
warn.arc.password_dropped: The new archive has no password
warn.arc.zip_aes: AES ZIP files don't open in every program (for example Windows Explorer)
desc.arc.split: Split into numbered parts .001, .002… (the original stays untouched)
err.arc.split_small: The file is smaller than {size}: no need to split it
err.arc.split_too_many: That would make {n} parts: choose a larger size
warn.arc.split_fat32: The parts are larger than 4 GB: they cannot be copied to a FAT32 drive
